reference: GNU ed 1.21.1 (Debian package ed 1.21.1-1, /usr/bin/ed in the runner reference PATH), run black-box and compared for stdout, stderr where marked exact, exit status and the resulting files. The bash type/help cases are contracts on the builtin's own metadata.
coverage: Bash type and help metadata for the static ed builtin and its synopsis/documented command set.
Bash type and help metadata for the ed builtin and its GNU synopsis.
Every existing POSIX case is now compared with GNU ed (parity) instead of a hand-written expectation.
Addresses, m/t/j/u, G/V, repeated s, file commands, shell escapes, y/x, z/n, quit warnings, -E/-l/-r, script-file errors, NUL bytes and usage errors.
exclusions: Terminal sessions (prompt echo, interrupts, the modified-buffer warning at a tty) are covered by the parity-vm terminal suites.

cases.purpose: Bash type metadata must identify ed as a builtin when PATH is empty.
cases.script:
[[ $(type -t ed) == builtin ]]
printf 'builtin\n'

cases.purpose: The Bash help entry shows the GNU ed synopsis and documents the script-file and exit-status rules.
cases.script:
doc=$(help ed)
[[ $doc == *'ed [-EGlqrsv] [-p PROMPT] [--strip-trailing-cr] [FILE | !COMMAND]'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'Edit text with the standard line editor.'* ]]
[[ $doc == *'When standard'*'input is a file, the first error ends ed.'* ]]
printf 'help metadata ok\n'

cases.purpose: POSIX ed append plus n and = commands print line numbers and text in their specified forms.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
alpha
beta
.
1,2n
2=
w sink.txt
q
ED

cases.purpose: POSIX BRE substitution with g and replacement '&' must replace each match with the matched text surrounded by angle brackets.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
id=7 id=42
.
1s/[0-9][0-9]*/<&>/g
1p
w sink.txt
q
ED

cases.purpose: Forward and backward regular-expression addresses wrap through the buffer, and a marked line remains addressable.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
red
blue
red
.
1ka
/blue/
?red?
'a
w sink.txt
q
ED

cases.purpose: The r command inserts a relative file after the current line; verify the resulting buffer text.
cases.script:
printf 'alpha\nbeta\n' > payload.txt
ed -s <<'ED'
a
head
.
r payload.txt
1,$p
w sink.txt
q
ED

cases.purpose: The w command creates a relative fixture file from the buffer; read it back with Bash builtins to verify bytes as lines.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
north
south
.
w saved.txt
q
ED
while IFS= read -r line; do printf '%s\n' "$line"; done < saved.txt
[[ $(<saved.txt) == $'north\nsouth' && $(/usr/bin/stat -c %s saved.txt) == 12 ]]

cases.purpose: Undo restores the line before the most recent substitution; the saved clean state also permits a normal quit.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
before
.
w saved.txt
s/before/after/
u
1p
q
ED

cases.purpose: The t command copies an addressed range after the destination, j joins addressed lines without a separator, and w persists the final buffer.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
red
blue
green
.
1,2t$
1,$p
4,5j
1,$p
w final.txt
q
ED
while IFS= read -r line; do printf 'file:%s\n' "$line"; done < final.txt
[[ $(<final.txt) == $'red\nblue\ngreen\nredblue' && $(/usr/bin/stat -c %s final.txt) == 23 ]]

cases.purpose: Check the editor's modified-buffer quit warning and response while attached to a terminal.
POSIX BRE replacement offsets and beginning-of-line anchors remain relative to the original line.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
xx1 y22 z333
.
1s/[0-9][0-9]*/<&>/g
1p
w output.txt
q
ED
[[ $(<output.txt) == "xx<1> y<22> z<333>" ]]

cases.purpose: POSIX BRE replacement offsets and beginning-of-line anchors remain relative to the original line.
cases.script:
ed -s <<'ED'
a
abc
.
1s/^/X/g
1p
w output.txt
q
ED
[[ $(<output.txt) == "Xabc" ]]

cases.purpose: Address forms: N . $ +N -N + - /RE/ ?RE? 'x , ; % offsets, an address followed by a number, and more than two addresses.
cases.script:

two
three
four
five
' > f

+
-
.+2
$-1
/f/
?t?
3kx
'"'"'x
,n
2;+1n
%%p
1 2p
1,2,3p
$=
.=
Q
' | ed -s f

two

four

,p

u

cases.purpose: G and V take one command per matching line from standard input, & repeats it, an empty line skips.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
five
' > f
printf 'G/o/
s/o/0/
&

V/o/
s/$/!/
&
,p
Q
' | ed -s f

cases.purpose: s alone repeats with toggled g/p and a count, r uses the last search, and \ splits a line.
cases.script:
printf 'oo1
oo2
oo3
oo4
' > f
printf '1s/o/O/
2sg
3s2
4sp
/3/
sr
1s/O/<\
>/
,l
Q
' | ed -s f || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: r, w, W, w with a range, e, E, f and the remembered file name.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
five
' > f
printf 'x
y
' > g
printf '2r g
1,2w h
4,5W h
f

printf '%s

cases.purpose: ! runs a shell command and prints !, r !cmd reads its output, w !cmd writes to it, !! repeats, and a command reading standard input gets the lines after it.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
five
' > f
printf '!echo hi
$r !echo there
1,2w !read a; read b; echo "$b $a"
!!
!read x; echo got "$x"
next line
,p
Q
after
' | { ed -s f; IFS= read -r rest; printf 'left: %s
' "$rest"; }

cases.purpose: y copies to the cut buffer and x puts it; d and c also fill it.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
five
' > f
printf '1,2y
$x
,p
3d
0x
,p
Q
' | ed -s f

cases.purpose: z prints a window from the next line, zN sets its size; n numbers lines.
cases.script:
seq 30 > f
printf '1z5
z
.=
25z
$n
Q
' | ed -s f

cases.purpose: q, e and Q on a modified buffer: the first q warns, a second q quits; Q never warns.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
five
' > f
printf '2d
q
q
' | ed -s f || echo rc=$?
printf '2d
e f
e f
,p
Q
' | ed -s f || echo rc=$?
printf '2d
Q
' | ed -s f || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: -E uses extended expressions; -l keeps status 0 after failed commands.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
five
' > f
printf ',s/(o|e)+/<&>/g
,p
/t(w|h)/p
Q
' | ed -sE f
printf '9p
Q
' | ed -sl f || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: -r refuses shell commands and file names with a slash.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
five
' > f
printf '!echo no
r /etc/passwd
h
w sub/x
h
Q
' | ed -rs f || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: With a script file, an error inside a g list ends ed and H names the line read so far.
cases.script:
printf 'one
two
three
four
five
' > f
printf 'H
g/o/s/o/0/\
99p
2p
' > sc
ed -s f < sc || echo rc=$?

cases.purpose: Lines holding NUL and high bytes are kept, listed with escapes and written back unchanged.
cases.script:
printf 'a\0b
\377\376
' > f
printf ',l
s/\x00/N/
,l
w g
q
' | ed -s f || echo rc=$?
od -c g

cases.purpose: An unknown option prints GNU ed's usage diagnostic and exits 1.
cases.script: ed -x < /dev/null || echo rc=$?
